title: Caerlum Rising Anew
premise: Mirabel Yarrow has spent three years erasing herself—no surname spoken, no debts owed, no name in any ledger—until a smuggler's job lands her with a century-old prophecy book that describes tonight's date, her scarred left hand, and the words 'the thirteenth moon shall find the door.' The door belongs to Caerlum, a kingdom unmade and unwritten from history after its last queen traded its existence for power; the prophecy's author was the queen's exiled scribe, and Mirabel is his heir. Hunted by the Chancellery of Records, which deletes people as easily as pages, and shadowed by Tam Vess, the smuggler whose loyalty she cannot afford to trust, Mirabel must gather the scattered fragments of Caerlum's true name before the thirteenth full moon. In the end she learns the door out of Caerlum opens only from inside it: to free herself she must enter the erased kingdom, refuse the crown offered to her as the scribe's bloodline, and speak Caerlum's name aloud—unmaking the Chancellery's power but binding herself forever to a country that exists only because she remembers it.
about_author: Astrid Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires in a northern university library before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people the record forgot, and lives off-grid with two ill-tempered goats and an annotated atlas of imaginary places.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Crimes
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She guides a smuggler's caravan through the Thornfell passes on the night of a full moon, trading on her knowledge of roads no map admits exist. When the cargo proves to be a sealed book rather than brandy, she pockets it out of habit. Emotional beat: wary competence masking loneliness—the reader meets a woman expert at being no one.

chapters.title: A Date Written Before Her Birth
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. By lamplight she opens the book and finds tonight's date heading a page describing a red-haired thief with a scarred left hand crossing the Thornfell under a full moon. The handwriting matches notes in her dead master's effects. Emotional beat: vertigo—the invisible life she built revealed as a line someone else wrote first.

chapters.title: What the Chancellery Burns
chapters.summary: Tam Vess's POV. The caravan's buyer, a Chancellery auditor named Corvane, arrives early and burns a village's parish records to erase a debtor. Tam watches Mirabel lie smoothly to him and realizes she is already on some list. Emotional beat: dread establishing the antagonist's method—power exercised as deletion, not violence.

chapters.title: The Hedge-Witch's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, with flashback. She returns to her late master Odara's ruined cottage and finds the prophecy book's marginalia in Odara's hand alongside an older script. A hidden letter names Mirabel heir to 'the Scribe of Caerlum' and warns her never to let the book be read aloud. Emotional beat: grief curdling into betrayal—her mentor knew and hid this.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons, Twelve Gone
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Deciphering the prophecy's calendar, she calculates the deadline: the coming moon is the thirteenth turn since the book's sealing. Corvane's riders reach the valley. She flees with the book and Odara's bones-in-a-box, meeting Tam on the road by arrangement neither will call trust. Emotional beat: the clock starts; flight becomes quest.

chapters.title: The Cartographer Who Drew Nothing
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. They seek Ilexa Quill, a disgraced royal cartographer living drunk in a fen town, who once mapped a border that officially never existed. Ilexa confirms Caerlum was real—and was 'recorded out' a century ago by the Chancellery's founding act. Emotional beat: bitter comedy giving way to horror at how completely a nation can be unwritten.

chapters.title: Fragments of a Name
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Ilexa explains the mechanism: Caerlum persists wherever its name survives—in songs, boundary stones, a lullaby's nonsense syllables. The prophecy's 'door' needs those fragments gathered. First fragment: a millstone carved with half the royal seal, guarded by a records-wight. Emotional beat: hope with a price—every fragment they take makes them louder.

chapters.title: Songs the Reapers Still Sing
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In a harvest village they collect the second fragment hidden in a work song's forgotten verse, and Mirabel feels the words physically pull toward something eastward. Corvane arrives hours behind them and hangs the reeve for withholding information. Emotional beat: guilt—her quest is now leaving bodies, testing whether truth justifies its cost.

chapters.title: Tam's Price
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Revealed: Tam sold word of Mirabel's route to Corvane months ago to buy his brother out of a debtors' ledger—before he knew what she carried. He tries to confess, fails, and instead misdirects Corvane at real risk. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth turned inward; the reader knows what Mirabel doesn't.

chapters.title: The Library That Eats Its Readers
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The third fragment lies in the Chancellery's own archive, inside the confiscated original of the Scribe's journal. Mirabel infiltrates as a junior clerk and reads her ancestor's account of Queen Sorrel's bargain: the queen traded Caerlum's recorded existence for immortality outside the page. Emotional beat: revelation reframing everything—the villain may be a victim still alive somewhere.

chapters.title: Corvane Offers Her a Pen
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Caught in the archive, Mirabel expects torture; instead Corvane offers apprenticeship. Deletion, he argues, is mercy—an end to debt, war, and being written by others. He shows her her own file: three years of careful invisibility, annotated in his hand. Emotional beat: temptation articulated so well she wavers; power's corruption begins as an offer of safety.

chapters.title: Escape Through the Unwritten Quarter
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam burns his brother's debt file to trigger an archive evacuation and pulls Mirabel out through a district the Chancellery never bothered mapping. In the chaos she finds he knew Corvane's face too well. Emotional beat: action set-piece braided with dawning suspicion; escape bought with a secret half-spent.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Fen Camp
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She confronts Tam with what she saw. He confesses fully; she walks into the marsh alone, then returns at dawn—not forgiving, but choosing him as the only witness to her quest. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh; loyalty chosen with eyes open, not innocence assumed.

chapters.title: The Queen Outside the Page
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Following the fragments' pull, they find Queen Sorrel alive in a hollow valley, unaged, tending a garden of plants that don't exist. Sorrel claims she erased Caerlum to save it from a conquering empire, and that restoration means her death. Emotional beat: sympathy for the antagonist; every certainty about the bargain inverted.

chapters.title: Sorrel's Version of the Truth
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Sorrel shows them the empire's invasion plans preserved in amber memory: Caerlum would have burned entire. But Tam notices the memory is curated—edited like any record. Sorrel is not lying; she is the Chancellery's first editor. Emotional beat: unease—even victims corrupt when they hold the pen alone.

chapters.title: The Door in the Boundary Stone
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. With all fragments gathered, the boundary stone on Thornfell's highest pass opens onto a grey country where roads remember being walked. Caerlum exists here as echo: empty halls, warm hearths, voices mid-sentence. The prophecy's final lines appear in the book in fresh ink. Emotional beat: awe and homesickness for a home she never had.

chapters.title: Inside the Erased Kingdom
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Within Caerlum's echo, Mirabel experiences the recorded-out dead as presences, including the Scribe himself, who explains the choice ahead: speak the name and restore Caerlum at the cost of anchoring herself to it forever—or walk out the far door and let it fade. Emotional beat: the trap of identity—to claim who she is, she must give up escape.

chapters.title: Corvane Crosses Over
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV (first use). He enters Caerlum with a company of auditors to delete the echo at its source, revealing his true aim: not order, but sole custody of what is remembered. Inside, deletion works both ways—the kingdom begins editing his auditors. Emotional beat: the antagonist's philosophy devouring its believers; horror of power unchecked.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon Rises
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Under the full moon, Sorrel arrives begging Mirabel to leave the name unspoken so she can live; Corvane demands she surrender the fragments; Tam stands with her against both. The Scribe's voice offers her the crown of Caerlum as the price of speaking. Emotional beat: climax of converging pressures—identity, power, loyalty all demanding payment at once.

chapters.title: Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She refuses the crown, refuses Sorrel's bargain, and speaks Caerlum's full name with Tam and the gathered fragments as witnesses. The kingdom floods back into the world—maps rewriting, stones remembering—while Sorrel ages into dust with something like relief, and Corvane is recorded out by his own collapsing Chancellery. Emotional beat: triumphant, costly climax; truth spoken costs everything except itself.

chapters.title: What Remains Written
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Aftermath: Caerlum restored but poor, its people returning from diaspora with no memory of why they always sang that lullaby. Mirabel, bound to the land, takes the modest office of Keeper of Records—with rules she writes herself, Tam as her first sworn witness. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning; power accepted with limits, love chosen without guarantees.

chapters.title: A New Page
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, epilogue. One year later, Mirabel adds the first entry to Caerlum's new chronicle: honest, dated, signed. She visits Odara's grave within the kingdom's borders at last, leaves the prophecy book open to a blank final page, and walks home down a road every map now admits exists. Emotional beat: resolution and gentle forward motion—the invisible woman visible, the story hers to write.
